The psychology of visibility ✨

Looking through the lens of human behaviour, it is against our biology to be seen, to be visible. 

Humans are pack animals. Our survival instinct tells us to fit in or we’ll be kicked out of the tribe.

But sometimes, certain things or periods in life require us to become more visible. To get to where we need to go. 

For most of my career, I spoke publicly. 

PS; I was not a public speaker before that. I was the type person who’d face would go as red as a tomato 🍅 

I did it because I had a passion for learning and helping people, the role just so happened to be at the front of the room. 

“If this is what I need to do to get to where in need to go, then I guess we’re doing it” — I used to tell myself to psych myself up some days. 

Something I learnt as I grew in my role was that visibility can bring up the all kinds of thoughts and fears that encourage us to stay small. 

Fear of judgement.
Fear of failure.
Fear of rejection.
Fear of being misunderstood.

So we adapt.

We manage perceptions.
We seek approval.
We edit our expression.
We become who we think we need to be to belong.

And sometimes, without realising it, we begin confusing acceptance with authenticity.

This is where self-leadership becomes important.

Because the goal isn’t to become someone who no longer experiences fear, anxiety or self-doubt.

It’s to develop the capacity to experience those emotions without allowing them to determine who we are or how we show up.

✔️ Stronger relationships

The Bagel story is a popular lesson shared by @simonsinek a thought leader in the world of mindset. 

*The story goes like this*

Simon and a friend were at a run event where bagels were being given out for free at the end. Simon wanted a bagel, but his friend complained about the long line. Simon’s perspective was that the bagel was free, so the line was worth it, while his friend fixated on the inconvenience of waiting. 

Simon saw the *opportunity* (a free bagel), whereas his friend saw only the *obstacle* (the line).

The lesson behind this story is about mindset 🧠

Some people focus on what they can gain (the opportunity) and are willing to endure the small inconveniences or challenges to get there, while others focus on the obstacles and let them hold them back from even trying.

I love this story because it’s a great example of how perspective influences our behaviour and results. 

Do you focus on obstacles or possibilities?

Every new thing you see in the world is because someone said no to an old story and chose to write something new.

MYTH: your business idea needs to be unique to be successful ❌

I’m definitely not the only business & alignment coach out there 🌎

Sure, we may have titled ourselves different names, but under the title, the idea is similar. 

〰️ to support people to be the best version of themselves in both life & business.

Many people in the online service-provider space will share that similar value. 

When you run a business aligned to your values, passions & skills you will find people who share similar ideas 💡 

& that is more than ok! ✨

My first launch generated over 5 figures a few months after being made redundant. 

How did I do it? 

I combined my corporate skills with my passion, my why and started teaching and supporting others to find their why & do the same. 

Some may have thought I was crazy to leave the corporate world and start my own business during a pandemic 😷 

But from my perspective; I saw it as the great awakening. A world event that caused people to think differently about how they want to live and what they want to do for a living 👩🏽‍💻 

People are looking for more fulfilment and to thrive in life, rather than just work to survive.

So, if you have been thinking about starting a side hustle, going full time or expanding your business here’s my reminder to you: 

👉🏼 It’s not so much about how “original” your idea is and more about how you bring it to life with your unique energy and the way you execute it. 

The best way to find out what is in alignment for you is to just start ✔️

MINI TRAINING: the art of communication + tips on how to communicate with influence ✨

Communication is an art, and the truth is that you can tell more about a persons feelings through non verbal cues like body language and tone of voice than their words.

Communication is broken down like this; 
✖️ 7% your words
✖️ 38% your tone 
✖️ 55% your body language 

I first learnt about this in the beginning of 2012. 

🏦 I remember it so well because it was at the very beginning of my career. 

My first job was in personal bank taking service enquires over the phone. We quickly learnt that a big component of communication was taken away (body language) so we could only use out tone and words to ensure the customer had a good experience. 

Throughout the rest of my career, communication played a big part. I not only facilitated sessions around sales & leadership conversations, I also used the skill each day, running those workshops. 

After many years trying all different ways to engage, interact with & motivate people, my best tip is to think about your style of communication; 

✖️ spoken (face to face/ phone?)
✖️ written 

And think about where you need to be spending your energy ✨

My journey from redundancy to my first 5-figure launch ✨🚀

When I first started my online coaching business, I thought people would want the professional me.

Well, that’s what almost 10 years in the corporate world taught me anyway.

I hid my authentic self behind my professionalism because I was scared that if I was just myself, I wouldn’t attract any clients, or worse, lose the ones I had.

Turns out, people want you in your zone of genius - yes, that’s what they’re paying you for 💸

But they also want your energy, authenticity and vulnerability ✨

The wonderful truth of being your own boss is that you get to decide how “professional” you want to be, that works for both you & your clients!
